messages:
anya: Heads-up — after the gpu-operator 2.6.0 rollout in us-west-2 this morning, we started seeing SGX-like scheduling churn on a subset of g4dn nodes. Pods requesting GPUs go Pending with GPUAllocatable=0 and then fail.
anya: Short log from the node: `Kernel module mismatch: nvidia.ko v525 vs kernel 5.10.81-1` and device-plugin shows `Advertise failed: driver not responding`.
kyle: ugh. did operator rebuild drivers or switch to new image that expects dkms?
devops-bot: deploy pipeline: gpu-operator image: nv/gpu-operator:2.6.0 -> rolled to nodepool-gpu-2 (12 nodes) at 06:12 UTC. No automatic rollback triggered.
maria: we're also seeing NCCL tests failing in CI that run on the same pool — ring init times out. Could be driver ABI mismatch.
anya: repro steps I ran: `kubectl describe pod gpu-test -n ci` -> `Warning  FailedScheduling  30s (x3)  device-plugin  No GPUs available` then on node: `dmesg | grep nvidia` shows `nvidia: module version 525 does not match kernel`
alex: Are those nodes running a custom kernel? which AMI?
anya: some nodes are on amazon-linux2-ami-2022.10, but three nodes in that pool were auto-upgraded by nodepool to kernel 5.15 last week (on-prem had custom kernel). Looks like operator image assumes headers present for dkms build.
kyle: if dkms couldn't build, driver falls back to module in the image, but if kernel API changed it's incompatible. Suggest cordon/evict and put those nodes in maintenance.
sre-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-344 gpu-driver-scheduling-usw2, severity: P2. Paging oncall.
maria: quick mitigation: set device-plugin to advertise only nodes with label `gpu-ready=true` and roll back 2.6.0 -> 2.5.8?
anya: I tried a targeted rollback on one nodepool: patched daemonset image to nv/gpu-operator:2.5.8, it started driver install but then DKMS failed with `no kernel headers found`
alex: check `/lib/modules/$(uname -r)/build` symlink. If node was booted into a different kernel than headers, DKMS fails.
kyle: can we temporarily taint nodes with `gpu-unusable=true:NoSchedule` until we have a proper fix? That avoids mass restart of workloads.
anya: doing that now on 3 nodes: `kubectl taint nodes node-gpu-12 gpu-unusable=true:NoSchedule`
anya: also adding cordon on the rest: `kubectl cordon node-...`
maria: for CI, switching test runners to a fallback pool without GPUs for now. Cost will increase due to CPU runners but at least pipelines move. :grimacing:
alex: Long-term fix options: 1) ensure node image includes kernel-devel/headers matching current kernel (AMI bake). 2) change operator to use precompiled driver matching kernel (maintain image per kernel). 3) prevent node auto-kernel upgrades on GPU pool.
sre-bot: Note: autoscaler drained 2 nodes due to failed readiness checks, new nodes launched with AMI id ami-0b57c8f3 in us-west-2. Check launch configuration.
devops-bot: Launch config for nodepool-gpu-2: AMI=ami-0b57c8f3, kernel 5.10, cloud-init script installs kernel-headers via yum.
anya: I'm attaching quick output (paste):
```
$ kubectl get nodes -l gpu=true -o wide
node-11   Ready,SchedulingDisabled   g4dn.xlarge   5.15.0-1021-aws
node-12   Ready                      g4dn.xlarge   5.10.81-1
node-13   NotReady                   g4dn.xlarge   5.15.0-1021-aws
```
and device-plugin log excerpt:
```
E0321 06:20:12.123456 1 plugin.go:214] Advertise failed: driver not responding: context deadline exceeded
```
```
DKMS error: cannot find kernel headers for 5.15.0-1021-aws
```

anya: Proposal: rollback operator in the pool + temporarily pin nodes to kernels we support, plus a one-off repair job that installs matching headers and re-runs DKMS.
kyle: +1 for repair job. Who can run it for the three affected nodes? I'll coordinate taints.
maria: I can run the repair steps in the morning window. Need SSH access; will open an Ops ticket for cross-team approval.
alex: Also update fleet bake to include `kernel-headers` package and lock auto-upgrade. I'll send PR to infra-images repo.
sre-bot: Next steps: 1) triage threads + root-cause doc 2) schedule maintenance window 3) bake AMI with headers 4) operator change to detect missing headers and mark node `gpu-ready=false`.
anya: I'll collect logs into INC-2026-344 and drop commands, steps we ran. Thanks all — will ping when repair is done. :thumbsup:
